headline: Immutable self-sovereign OVMs and splits; no upgrade path or central admin over user validators/funds; DAO governance limited to T3/T4 collective decisions

findings.text: ObolValidatorManagerFactory (mainnet 0x2c26B5A373294CaccBd3DE817D9B7C6aea7De584) and ImmutableSplitControllerFactory have no owner/admin view methods; OVMs deployed with owner set by caller (typically user/SAFE multisig) who grants RBAC roles. No central protocol owner. (from defipunkd surfacer + docs)

All core contracts (factories, OVMs, splits, ImmutableSplitController) are explicitly immutable/non-upgradeable with no proxy patterns or upgrade functions. Self-sovereign design. (docs.obol.org/learn/readme/obol-splits + GitHub repo)

No execution path/timelock for upgrades on core contracts; per-deployment OVM control is immediate via owner/RBAC. DAO governance (OBOL token + Governor on Tally) handles collective treasury/incentives only.
No reachable multisigs on core upgrade/execution path; per-OVM owner (user-controlled SAFE recommended) holds scoped RBAC (DEPOSIT_ROLE, WITHDRAWAL_ROLE, etc.). No emergency or protocol-wide pause.
OBOL token governance via Tally (Token House) for DAO proposals; no on-chain reads performed on Governor constants this run (corroborated by docs and Tally page).
No separate emergency powers; all actions user-controlled via OVM owner/RBAC.

Highest tier reachable is T3 (governance-internal: DAO treasury/params) or T4 (operational); T1/T2 unreachable on immutable cores holding user funds/validators. (docs explicitly state self-sovereign, no third-party upgrade control)

steelman.red: A single EOA or 2-of-3 could control upgrades to user validator contracts and drain funds.
steelman.orange: Governance or multisig could reach T2 economic parameters with short/no timelock.
steelman.green: Immutable non-upgradeable contracts with self-sovereign per-deployment owner control make T1/T2 unreachable; DAO limited to non-fund-critical decisions.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because immutable self-sovereign OVMs/splits (C2+C7) eliminate any admin upgrade or fund-drain path, with only T3/T4 DAO governance reachable; strongest steel-man is green.

evidence.shows: ObolValidatorManagerFactory has no owner/admin; deploys OVMs with caller-set owner and no proxy/upgrade functions
ImmutableSplitControllerFactory creates immutable controllers; no owner/admin exposed
Contracts are immutable, non-upgradeable, self-sovereign; permissioned actions controlled by deployer/owner only; no third-party upgrade access
Public repo with contracts; confirms mainnet deployments and immutable design (v0.4 release)
evidence.commit: main branch (no specific SHA pinned for this run)

evidence.shows: OBOL governance token; MINTER_ROLE and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE visible (admin set to zero in some cases)

unknowns: C5: exact Governor votingPeriod/quorum/timelock constants not re-read on-chain via /api/contract/read this run (docs/Tally corroboration only)

protocol_metadata.about: Obol provides Distributed Validator Technology (DVT) for Ethereum staking. Users/staking pools deploy self-sovereign Obol Validator Managers (via factory) as withdrawal recipients to split rewards/principal, rotate keys, and manage exits in distributed validator clusters using Charon middleware. Immutable splits enable non-custodial reward distribution. OBOL token enables DAO governance for the Obol Collective.

headline: Self-sovereign OVMs allow owner/RBAC-controlled withdrawals/exits with no central pause; follows Ethereum native exit queues

findings.text: Key exit functions in ObolValidatorManager: withdraw() (partial/full via EIP-7002), consolidate() for key rotation.
WITHDRAWAL_ROLE (or owner) gates withdraw/exit; DEPOSIT_ROLE for deposits. No protocol-wide pause guards; per-OVM RBAC.
No PAUSE_ROLE or indefinite pause; roles are set/controlled by OVM owner (self-sovereign).
No emergency/governance pause distinction; all actions user-controlled.
Queued redemptions follow Ethereum withdrawal queue (~27h partial, ~5d full exit); queue itself not pausable by protocol.
No need for forced-escape hatch; owner/RBAC directly controls withdrawals/exits.
Exits callable directly on-chain (Etherscan write tab or wallet) without frontend; factories permissionless.

steelman.red: Central admin could pause all claims indefinitely or require signatures for exits.
steelman.orange: Indefinite governance pause on finalized claims or long queues >7d.
steelman.green: Fully permissionless per-OVM owner/RBAC exits with no protocol pause; follows native Ethereum queues.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because OVMs grant self-sovereign WITHDRAWAL_ROLE/owner control over exits with no pause (E2+E3+E7); strongest steel-man is green.

evidence.shows: OVM withdraw() gated by WITHDRAWAL_ROLE/owner; no pause; self-sovereign; funds available after Ethereum exit queue
Factory deploys OVMs with owner-set roles for withdrawals

unknowns: E3: exact role hashes and current pause state not re-read on a live deployed OVM instance this run (per-deployment)

headline: No material external dependencies; oracle-free, immutable contracts; failures limited to chosen cluster operators (mitigated by DVT diversification)

findings.text: No oracle/price feed/external contract calls in core OVMs/splits; oracle-free by design (docs).
Operator risk is base Ethereum substrate + DVT cluster (diversified nodes/clients); no small curated set with principal-loss propagation.
No cross-chain bridges or messaging dependencies for core flows.
No nested collateral/restaking; direct Ethereum validators.
DVT design itself is fallback (multi-node fault tolerance); no external fallbacks needed as core is self-contained.
No keeper/relayer liveness required for core validator management/exits.
Immutable contracts prevent governance from swapping any external dependencies.

steelman.red: Single external oracle or bridge failure could drain principal.
steelman.orange: Unmitigated keeper liveness or mutable dependency could degrade yield/performance.
steelman.green: Pure on-chain Ethereum staking infrastructure with no oracles/bridges/keepers; DVT provides built-in resilience; zero impacted TVS from external failure.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because core contracts are oracle-free and immutable with no external call dependencies (A1+A6+A9); DVT mitigates operator risk; strongest steel-man is green.

evidence.shows: Oracle-free, no external dependencies, self-sovereign immutable design
Contracts confirm no oracle integrations or mutable external calls

unknowns: A2: exact diversification stats/TVS per cluster not quantified on-chain this run (DVT docs claim resilience)

headline: Permissionless factory deployment of OVMs/splits; no whitelists/KYC; direct on-chain calls possible

findings.text: No whitelist/allowlist/onlyRole on factory createObolValidatorManager or core user actions beyond per-OVM RBAC set by owner.
No off-chain operators required for admission; factories permissionless.
Direct contract interaction via wallets/aggregators/Etherscan write tab; GitHub SDKs and third-party integrations (e.g., Lido CSM, EtherFi) exist independently.
Read access fully permissionless; writes permissionless at factory level (per-OVM RBAC is user choice).

steelman.red: Contract-level KYC/whitelist or single-operator approval gates entry/exit.
steelman.orange: Contracts open but no independent paths beyond official frontend.
steelman.green: Fully permissionless factory + direct on-chain access with independent paths (wallets, third-party staking products).

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because factories are permissionless with no whitelists and independent access paths exist (A1+A3b); frontend ToS irrelevant to contracts.

evidence.shows: Permissionless creation of OVMs via factory; self-sovereign; no KYC/whitelists mentioned
createObolValidatorManager is public write function with no access gates
